oneSentence: An organised set of trusted documents that a search system can look through to find relevant passages for an answer.
plainExplanation:
A knowledge base is the collection of material a system searches when it needs source text. It might include policies, manuals, reports, FAQs or approved web pages. The key idea is that the collection is chosen and maintained for a purpose, not gathered at random.

What goes in: documents or passages that an organisation wants to use as reference material. These are often cleaned, split into smaller pieces and indexed. An index is a structure that helps the system find useful parts quickly.

What happens: when someone asks a question, the system searches the knowledge base for passages that seem relevant. In modern systems, this may use semantic search, which looks for similar meaning rather than only matching exact words. The selected passages can then be shown directly or passed to a language model to help draft an answer with sources.

What comes out: ideally, a smaller set of relevant passages, and sometimes an answer grounded in those passages. This is different from training. Putting a document into a knowledge base does not usually change the model's parameters; it gives the system something to look up at answer time.

everydayAnalogy.title: The shelf of official binders at a distribution point
everydayAnalogy.story: At a food distribution point, the team keeps a shelf of labelled binders: delivery schedules, stock rules, ration tables and site procedures. When a new staff member asks, "How much rice should a household of five receive this month?", the supervisor does not rely on memory alone. They pull the relevant binder, open the right section and read out the current rule. The shelf is not every paper in the building; it is the set of documents the team has chosen to rely on for this job.

everydayAnalogy.limitation: A real knowledge base is usually digital, can search thousands of passages in seconds and may use meaning-based matching rather than a person reading tabs by hand. Also, people can judge context more flexibly than a simple search system. The analogy helps with the idea of a trusted reference collection, but it does not show embeddings, ranking or the risk of retrieving the wrong passage.

visual.title: How a knowledge base supports an answer
visual.learningObjective: Show that a knowledge base is the maintained document collection a system searches before returning passages or a grounded answer.
visual.description: A left-to-right flow with four boxes. First, selected documents enter the system. Next, the documents are organised for search. Then a user question triggers retrieval of relevant passages. Finally, the system outputs passages, or an answer with citations. Read from left to right to see what goes in, what happens and what comes out.

steps.label: 1. Collect trusted material
steps.explanation: Choose the documents to include, such as policies, manuals, reports or FAQs. The value of the knowledge base depends on what is included and what is left out.
steps.visualInstruction: Show a box on the left containing 5 to 7 document icons labelled with examples like policy, manual, report and FAQ. Add a small badge saying selected sources.

steps.label: 2. Prepare for search
steps.explanation: The documents are often cleaned, split into smaller passages and indexed so the system can search them quickly.
steps.visualInstruction: Show the document box feeding into a processing box with three small icons: broom for cleaning, scissors for splitting, and card index for indexing. Use arrows to indicate transformation.

steps.label: 3. Match the question to passages
steps.explanation: When a question arrives, the system searches the knowledge base to find the passages that seem most relevant by words, meaning or both.
steps.visualInstruction: Place a user question bubble above an arrow into a search box. Inside the search box, highlight three passage cards pulled from the indexed collection. Mark them ranked 1, 2 and 3.

steps.label: 4. Return evidence or support an answer
steps.explanation: The output may be the passages themselves, or those passages may be handed to a language model to help draft an answer with citations.
steps.visualInstruction: Show two possible outputs on the right: one panel with highlighted passages, and one panel with a short answer linked by citation markers to those passages.

visual.interaction: Hovering or tapping each stage highlights what changes at that step; selecting the final stage toggles between 'passages only' and 'answer with citations'.
visual.accessibilityDescription: The diagram shows a four-stage process from left to right. Stage one is a selected set of trusted documents, such as policies, manuals, reports and FAQs. Stage two shows those documents being cleaned, split into smaller passages and indexed for search. Stage three adds a user question and shows the system retrieving and ranking several relevant passages from the collection. Stage four shows two possible outputs: either the retrieved passages are shown directly, or they are used to support an answer that includes citations back to the source passages. The point is that the knowledge base is the maintained document collection that search uses before any answer is produced.
visual.reducedMotionDescription: A static four-column diagram replaces animation. Column one shows selected documents. Column two shows preparation steps: cleaning, splitting and indexing. Column three shows a question linked to three ranked passages. Column four shows either passages only or an answer with citations, displayed side by side.

workedExample.scenario: A municipal help desk uses a knowledge base of approved public service documents to answer resident questions.
workedExample.input: Question: "Can I renew my parking permit online if I moved to a new address?"
process: The knowledge base contains the parking permit policy, the online renewal guide and a page about proof-of-address requirements.
The documents were split into short passages and indexed for search.
The system retrieves three top passages: one on renewals, one on address changes and one on required documents.
A response tool uses those passages to draft a short answer and attaches citations to the relevant sections.
workedExample.result: Output: "Online renewal is available, but if your address has changed you may need to update your details and provide new proof of address before the permit is reissued." The answer cites the renewal guide and the proof-of-address section.

unWorkplaceExample.scenario: A protection analysis team wants to identify broad trends across incident reports by searching a vetted internal collection of approved, access-controlled documents and summaries.
unWorkplaceExample.relevance: A well-maintained knowledge base helps staff find previous reporting, guidance and standard definitions quickly, which can improve consistency and save time before human review.
unWorkplaceExample.caution: Do not place personal data, survivor information, witness details, security-sensitive material or other confidential records into an unapproved public AI service. Use only authorised systems, apply access controls and keep human oversight over interpretation and reporting.

whyItMatters: For non-specialists, the knowledge base often determines whether an AI-supported answer is useful, outdated or unsupported. If the collection is incomplete, poorly maintained or includes low-quality documents, the system may retrieve weak evidence and produce misleading output. If the collection is well chosen and current, staff can find relevant passages faster, check sources more easily and make better decisions about whether to trust or reject an answer. In other words, the knowledge base is a governance issue as much as a technical one: what you include, who maintains it and how current it is all shape the quality of the result.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: A knowledge base is the same thing as the AI model's memory.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Not usually. The knowledge base is an external collection of documents the system can search at answer time. The model is a separate component. Adding a document to the knowledge base does not normally retrain the model or guarantee the model will repeat that document without retrieval.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: If a document is in the knowledge base, the answer will automatically be correct.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Inclusion helps, but it does not guarantee a good result. The system still has to retrieve the right passage, rank it well and use it accurately. Poor chunking, weak indexing, outdated documents or unclear questions can still lead to an unsupported answer.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: A vector database and a knowledge base are the same thing.
commonMisconceptions.correction: They are related but different. A knowledge base is the content collection itself: the documents or passages chosen as sources. A vector database is one possible tool for storing numerical representations of that content to support meaning-based search.

simpleVsTechnical.simple: Think of it as the approved shelf of documents a system looks through before answering a question.
simpleVsTechnical.technical: In retrieval systems, a knowledge base is the curated corpus of source documents used for lookup at inference time. Documents are typically normalised, split into chunks, indexed and sometimes converted into embeddings, which are numerical representations used to compare meaning. A retriever searches this corpus by keywords, semantic similarity or both, and returns candidate passages. Those passages may then be reranked and either shown directly or supplied to a language model in a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline. The knowledge base is therefore the content layer, distinct from the search index, the vector database that may store embeddings, and model training, which changes model parameters rather than providing external source material at query time.

keyTakeaway: A knowledge base is the trusted document collection behind search and grounded answers, so its quality strongly shapes the quality of the result.

quickCheck.question: Which description best fits a knowledge base in a search or RAG system?
options: The internal weights of a model learned during training
A selected collection of source documents that the system searches for relevant passages
A list of questions users asked in the past
A tool that rewrites answers to sound more natural
quickCheck.explanation: Option 2 states the defining role: a selected source collection searched for relevant passages. Model weights come from training, a bare query history is not necessarily source material, and a rewriting tool changes wording rather than supplying sources.

issues.problem: Both fields make being "trusted" part of the definition. A knowledge base is defined by its role as a source collection, not by the reliability of its contents. The page itself later explains that a knowledge base may contain outdated or low-quality documents. The one-sentence definition also needs the search and RAG scope because "knowledge base" has broader uses elsewhere.
issues.fix: Use "In search and RAG, an organised source collection that a system searches to find relevant material for an answer." Replace "trusted document collection" in the takeaway with "selected source collection".

issues.problem: The result asserts policy details without showing what the retrieved passages say. It also names only the renewal and proof-of-address sections as citations, although the answer's claim about updating details appears to depend on the address-change passage.
issues.fix: Output: The renewal passage says online renewal is available. The address-change and proof-of-address passages say changed details and new proof may be required before reissue. The draft repeats those points and cites all three sections.

issues.problem: The caution addresses confidentiality but not the analytical risk created by the scenario. Retrieved passages are not necessarily representative of all incident reports, so search results alone cannot establish broad trends.
issues.fix: Use authorised systems with access controls. Never put personal, survivor, witness, security-sensitive or confidential records into an unapproved public AI service. Retrieved passages do not prove broad trends, so require human review before reporting.

issues.problem: The statement that a knowledge base is categorically separate from the history of user questions is false. Past questions could be included in a source collection if they were deliberately selected and indexed. Option 2 remains the best answer because it states the defining role, while option 3 merely names possible content without saying it is used as source material.
